mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes R 350 or 500 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M272 engine for the R 350 costs £2,800-£4,500 supply-only; a rebuilt M273 V8 for the R 500 costs £3,800-£6,800 supply-only. Fitting adds £800-£1,500 depending on complexity - V8 work requires specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of balance shaft failure on a Mercedes R 350?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check engine light with correlation codes P0018, P0019 and engine misfires are the classic warning signs on the M272 engine. This was a known issue across 2006-2007 Mercedes V6 models.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes R 350 or 500 petrol engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M272 V6 and M273 V8 are fundamentally strong engines, but have well-documented weaknesses. The M272 suffers from balance shaft wear on pre-2007 engines, while the M273 can develop timing chain guide degradation. With these addressed, both are capable of 150,000+ miles.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes R 350 and 500 petrol engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M272 and M273 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work is needed. Balance shaft issues on the M272 typically appear between 60,000-100,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes R 350 or 500 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the R Class is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt M272 costs £2,800-£4,500 - comparable to the value of a £3,000-£8,000 vehicle. The R 500's higher value (£4,000-£10,000) makes replacement even more justifiable for well-maintained examples.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes R 350 or 500 petrol need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies MB 229.5 high-performance oil - typically 5W-30 or 5W-40 fully synthetic. The M272 requires approximately 8.0 litres; the M273 requires approximately 9.0 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz R Class 350/500 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The R 350 and R 500 launched with the W251 generation in 2006 as the petrol V6 and V8 flagships of Mercedes' luxury MPV range. The R 350 was powered by the M272 3.5-litre V6 producing 272hp, while the early R 500 used the M113 5.0-litre V8 with 306hp. In 2007, the R 500 received the new M273 5.5-litre V8 with 388hp. Both variants offered refined, powerful petrol alternatives to the diesel range, with 4MATIC all-wheel drive available as standard on the R 500 and optional on the R 350.

milestones.description: M273.963, 5.5L V8 petrol, 388hp @ 6,000rpm (facelift R 500, replaces M113)
2012 - R 350 continues with M272; R 500 continues with M273 to end of UK production

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mercedes Benz R Class 350 and 500 petrol is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points - from M272 balance shaft wear to M273 timing chain guide degradation.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz R Class 350/500 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The R 350's M272 V6 and the R 500's M113/M273 V8s are refined, powerful petrol engines, but each has well-documented weaknesses that become more pronounced with age and mileage. The M272 is notorious for balance shaft sprocket wear on pre-2007 engines, while the M273 suffers from timing chain guide degradation. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: M272 Balance Shaft Sprocket Wear - The R 350's Critical Weakness
problems.rootCause: Early M272 V6 engines used a soft metal balance shaft sprocket that wears prematurely, causing timing correlation faults and engine misfires. This was a known issue across 2006-2007 Mercedes V6 models.

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - Balance shaft & timing chain replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full engine disassembly, replace balance shaft with updated gear, new timing chain, guides, tensioner

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt M272 with revised design
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Bench rebuild using updated factory-spec sprockets, new bearings, upgraded gaskets, supply & fit

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2006-2012 R 350 is worth approximately £3,000-£8,000 depending on condition. These luxury MPVs have suffered significant depreciation, meaning replacement costs can approach vehicle value for higher-mileage examples.
problems.recommendation: If your R 350 shows check engine light codes P0018, P0019 or misfire codes, have the balance shaft inspected immediately. The balance shaft replacement is a significant job, and we recommend opting for a complete rebuilt M272 unit featuring the revised sprocket design, which guarantees mechanical integrity.

problems.h4: M273 Timing Chain Guide Wear - The R 500 V8's Age-Related Failure
problems.rootCause: The M273 can suffer from timing chain guide degradation and tensioner wear. Chain guide fragments can enter the oil sump, causing catastrophic failure. Camshaft adjuster solenoid failure causing rough idle is also common.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, guides, tensioner, inspect camshaft adjusters
repairOptions.longevity: 70k-100k miles if caught before guide fragments enter sump

repairOptions.longevity: If guide fragments have damaged bearings

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2007-2012 R 500 is worth approximately £4,000-£10,000 depending on condition. The R 500's higher original specification means replacement remains justifiable for well-maintained examples.
problems.recommendation: If you hear timing chain rattle on cold start from your R 500, act immediately. The M273's timing chain guides are a known weakness with age. On an R 500 worth £4,000-£10,000, preventative timing chain replacement is always the better investment.
